title: Strong Leaders Always Defend Others From Unfair Criticism
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article argues that publicly defending team members from unfair outside criticism is among the most powerful ways a leader earns loyalty. Good leaders first gather context before responding, but then mount a visible, public defense regardless of the circumstances — even coaching the team member privately afterward if needed. When a leader can't defend the specific action taken, the piece argues they can still defend the person's character and value, separating judgment of behavior from respect for the individual. The article closes with the metaphor of watching someone's blind spot in a fight: any criticism aimed at a team member becomes, in effect, aimed at the leader too.
points: Publicly defending team members from unfair outside criticism is one of the most powerful ways leaders earn deep loyalty.
Good leaders gather context before responding but then mount a public defense regardless of the circumstances.
When a specific action can't be defended, leaders can still defend the person's underlying value and character.
The leader's code: any criticism aimed at a team member becomes a criticism the leader answers on their behalf.
quotes: good leaders...maintain a sharp eye for derogatory remarks, putdowns, and unfair feedback directed at their team members.
When team members know from experience that a leader will step in to set the record straight...they will be willing to walk through walls for that leader.
Leaders can always defend the quality and value of the person.
A leader can admire the person without condoning specific behavior.
Any slap directed at a team member becomes a slap aimed at them. They strike back in a supportive but professional way.
